## Context / Problem

There is a latent 4-hop import cycle in `src/rebar/llm/`, held open only by two deferred
(function-body) imports:

1. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:38` — `from rebar.llm.completion import
   verify_step_floor` — module level
2. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:43` — `from . import completion_banking as
   _bank` — module level
3. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:684` — `from .completion_recovery import
   CompletionAgentStep, raise_completion_workflow_failure` — inside a function
4. `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:446` — `from rebar.llm.workflow import gate_dispatch` —
   inside a function

`verify_step_floor` (`completion.py:235`) is a ~15-line arithmetic clamp over a `VerifyConfig`
(criteria count + direct-child count + 4 config fields -> an int). It is the only reason
`completion_banking.py` needs a module-level edge back into `completion.py`. Both deferred
imports are unmarked as cycle-breakers — tidying up either one (an ordinary refactor move)
silently breaks the package import at runtime. That invisibility, not the cycle itself, is the
cost: nothing flags these two imports as load-bearing.

**Verified by execution on `origin/main@2e28d817a7eefca3935a0ead4c84d584eda8c201`** (not by
reading): copied `src/` to scratch, used an `ast`-based hoist to move imports 3 and 4 to module
level, then imported:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'verify_step_floor' from partially initialized module
'rebar.llm.completion' (most likely due to a circular import)
  .../workflow/completion_recovery.py, in <module>: from . import completion_banking as _bank
  .../workflow/completion_banking.py, in <module>: from rebar.llm.completion import verify_step_floor
```

Hoisting import 4 alone imports cleanly — confirming import 4 alone does not close the loop;
both hoisted together reproduces the cycle.

## Approach

Move `verify_step_floor` and its constant `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` (`completion.py:67`) into
`src/rebar/llm/config.py`. `config.py` is the right home: the function's only non-literal input
is a `VerifyConfig`, so the clamp is a config-driven computation, and `config.py` does not
import `completion.py` (direct or transitive — confirmed by reading its import block), so the
move cannot recreate the cycle. `config.py` is 553 LOC; the move adds ~23 LOC, landing at ~576,
under the 800 cap.

`completion.py` re-imports `verify_step_floor` from `rebar.llm.config` at module level (joining
the existing `from rebar.llm.config import VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL, LLMConfig` line) so its own
call site (`:433`) still works and `completion.verify_step_floor` stays a resolvable module
attribute for the existing `monkeypatch.setattr(completion, "verify_step_floor", ...)` test
seam. `completion_banking.py:38` re-points to `rebar.llm.config`. With that edge gone, imports 3
and 4 both become ordinary module-level imports.

Moving the function out of `completion.py` has one mechanical consequence in the config schema.
Four `VerifyConfig` fields (`completion_verify_steps_per_criterion`,
`completion_verify_step_floor_min`, `completion_verify_child_traversal_steps`,
`completion_verify_fixed_overhead_steps`) are read only by `verify_step_floor`, so once it
leaves, `scripts/check_config_reads.py` no longer sees a read in the declaring module and fails.
The sanctioned remedy is that checker's own pointer marker: a `# read-via: llm/config.py
verify_step_floor` comment on each of the four fields. This is comment-only — no new config key,
no default change, no behaviour change — and adds no mechanism (`read-via` is an existing
documented escape hatch, not a new one).

**Verified by execution:** applied this move in the scratch copy, re-hoisted both edges, and
`import rebar.llm.completion, rebar.llm.workflow.gate_dispatch, rebar.llm` succeeded. A
whole-tree `pkgutil.walk_packages` sweep found only the 2 pre-existing `fastapi` import failures
also present in the unmodified tree. No new failure, no new cycle.

This moves **one function** to close **one cycle** — it does NOT hoist the ~258 other lazy
imports across `llm/`. A prior review tested that broader move and it was refuted: hoisting
binds the imported name at load time, so a later `monkeypatch.setattr` on the *original* source
module (the majority object-form pattern among ~2,900 patch sites) stops reaching the call
site — 4 regression files / 6 failing tests. This ticket touches exactly the two edges whose
cycle was reproduced above, and verifies each existing patch seam individually (see Testing).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — remove `verify_step_floor` (`:235`) and
  `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` (`:67`); add `verify_step_floor` to the existing config import line;
  hoist `from rebar.llm.workflow import gate_dispatch` (`:446`) to module level.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — add `verify_step_floor` + `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` (moved
  verbatim with their docstring/comment).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — comment-only: add four `# read-via: llm/config.py
  verify_step_floor` markers on the four `VerifyConfig` fields named in Approach, so
  `scripts/check_config_reads.py` still resolves a reader after the move. No schema, default,
  or behaviour change.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py` — re-point `:38`'s import to `rebar.llm.config`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — hoist the `completion_recovery` import (`:684`)
  to module level.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py` — re-point `:20`'s import to
  `rebar.llm.config`.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verdict_cache.py` — re-point the `:549` in-test import
  to `rebar.llm.config`.
- `tests/unit/test_completion_wrapper_duration_instrumentation.py` — no code change expected at
  `:455` (the `monkeypatch.setattr` seam survives via the re-import); verified by running the
  test, not by inspection alone.

## Testing

- Run the 3 directly affected test files and confirm all pass — the exhaustive set of
  non-source references to the moved symbols.
- Confirm `python -c "import rebar.llm.completion, rebar.llm.workflow.gate_dispatch, rebar.llm"`
  succeeds with both lazy imports hoisted to module level — the regression check for the cycle
  this ticket closes.
- Run `make verify` (lint + typecheck + import-convention guard + the full `not integration and
  not external` suite) and confirm it passes — this is what exercises
  `scripts/check_config_reads.py` against the four new `read-via` markers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `verify_step_floor` / `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX` are defined in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`
      and no longer in `completion.py`; checked by `grep -n "def verify_step_floor"` against
      each file (1 hit in `config.py`, 0 in `completion.py`).
- [x] `gate_dispatch.py`'s `completion_recovery` import and `completion.py`'s `gate_dispatch`
      import are both module-level (not inside a function body); checked by reading the diff.
- [x] `python -c "import rebar.llm.completion, rebar.llm.workflow.gate_dispatch, rebar.llm"`
      exits 0 from the worktree root with the venv active.
- [x] The 3 affected test files pass under the bare `pytest` console script.
- [x] `make verify` passes (lint, typecheck, import-convention guard, full suite).
- [x] No file in `src/rebar` exceeds 800 LOC after the change (checked by `wc -l`).
- [x] `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` carries a `# read-via: llm/config.py verify_step_floor`
      marker on each of the four `VerifyConfig` fields, and the change adds no new config key,
      default, or mechanism; checked by reading the diff and by `make verify` passing.
